To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) CE FIR equalization can be used to efficiently implement single-carrier communication with receiver oversampling in the presence of a large delay spread, (b) the CE equalizer can be efficiently implemented with a complexity of O(N log(N)), and (c) the CE equalization can be combined with CG algorithm to achieve even better performance.

the CE and CG methods can be applied in the context of single-carrier non-block transmission with receiver oversampling and that they can provide significant computational savings compared to block transmission schemes.

the CG equalizer with the appropriate stopping criteria is an efficient and reliable solution to the single-carrier equalization problem, and that the CG equalization can be implemented efficiently using FFTs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
efficient wideband single-carrier equalization.
efficient equalization of wideband single-carrier transmission schemes in the context of nonblock transmissions with receiver oversampling.
efficient equalization methods for single-carrier non-block transmission schemes.

for a given channel, a given data rate and a given oversampling factor, we can always choose a suitable equalization method and stopping criterion to obtain the optimal performance.
the CE and the conjugate gradient methods are efficient, simple, and reliable for equalization of single-carrier non-block transmission systems with receiver oversampling.
the proposed methods provide an attractive and efficient means for wideband single-carrier equalization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed efficient equalization techniques that are well suited for single-carrier communication over large-delay-spread wireless channels.

for single-carrier communication schemes with receiver oversampled transmission, the proposed CE equalizers can be used to achieve a high spectral efficiency and the proposed CG equalization can achieve a low computational complexity.
we have proposed efficient wideband single-carrier equalization algorithms for nonblock transmission schemes, and that we have shown the performance of the algorithms in various environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by using a simple FIR equalizer and the CG algorithm, we can obtain equalizers that are both computationally efficient and robust against noise.
the proposed methods can provide significant performance improvements over the MMSE equalizer at a very low computational cost.
the combination of the CE method and CG algorithm is an efficient means for wideband single-carrier equalization.
